about: Cars researched but held back from the game because one figure could not be sourced to the rules in docs/DATA_GUIDE.md. Nothing in this folder is loaded by the game or the validator.

cars.missing: A US curb weight from a qualifying source (manufacturer page, major magazine spec panel, or two independent editorial outlets that agree).

confirmed.powerQuote: The first M3 produced 192 hp from its 2.3-liter four-cylinder engine during its 1988-1991 model year run.

weightCandidates.source: Grassroots Motorsports project-car panel (auto-filled, contains errors)

cars.notes: BMW Group Classic gives production 1986-1990 and only the European 1,200 kg. 3 October 2026 provisional pass: weak sources disagree by about 4.8% (Carscoops, eightiescars, ultimatespecs about 2,735 lb; iSeeCars, Grassroots Motorsports, strictlyeta about 2,865 lb), so it stays held. 5 October 2026: ultimatespecs (owner) gives 2,734 lb / 1,240 kg for the M3 (US) 1988-1991, one more vote for ~2,735; the conflict with ~2,865 stays. Would resolve: a BMW of North America 1988-1991 M3 brochure or spec sheet, or a period Road & Track / Car and Driver spec panel with the US curb weight.

cars.missing: A curb weight from a second source or a magazine spec panel, and Ford's own release read on a Ford or press site (it was found only as a forum copy).

weightCandidates.source: duPont Registry (Edward Jones, 25 Jan 2024), not labelled curb

cars.notes: Hagerty's buyer's guide gives 2,027 cars for 2005 and 2,011 for 2006. 3 October 2026 provisional pass: weak sources disagree by about 4% (Edmunds 3,475 lb; Cars.com and KBB 3,350 lb; duPont Registry 3,485 lb unlabelled), so it stays held. 5 October 2026: AutoPadre (owner) gives 3,350 lb, unsourced, one more vote. A forum post says Ford's press-kit PDF lists 3,350 lb on page 21 (no link). Would resolve: Ford's 2005 GT press kit, or the 2006 Ford GT brochure at auto-brochures.com/makes/Ford/GT/Ford_US%20GT_2006.pdf (rate-limited when tried).

cars.missing: A settled curb weight and US model years. Three kerb figures exist: 1,480 kg (Evo panel, used in the draft), 1,365 kg (usually attributed to Ferrari, seen only in auto-filled panels) and 3,230 lb (Hagerty, US car). The draft record is EU-market with calendar years 2002-2004, unlike the other Ferraris; US model years were not sourced.
cars.notes: 660 cv = 651 hp (ferrari.com magazine article). 6-speed automated manual, V12 5,998 cc, dry weight 1,255 kg per Ferrari. 3 October 2026 provisional pass: two named-author outlets (auto.cz, Michal Razim; km77, Victor M. Fernandez) give a kerb weight of 1,365 kg, which conflicts with Evo's panel figure of 1,480 kg (8% apart, both step 2); stays held until one is shown to be right. US model year appears to be 2003 only (EPA via MPG Buddy, Hagerty). 5 October 2026: ultimatespecs (owner) gives 1,365 kg curb and 1,255 kg dry; Supercars.net 1,365 and 1,370 kg; forcar.org page not found. Still two camps (1,365 vs Evo 1,480 / Hagerty US 3,230 lb). Would resolve: Ferrari's 2002 Enzo press kit with a kerb weight, or a 2003 US road test (Road & Track, Car and Driver, Motor Trend) giving curb weight.

cars.missing: A qualifying curb weight. Ferrari's release gives no weight, and the four magazine figures found disagree.

confirmed.powerQuote: Total maximum power: 963 CV (Ferrari Geneva 2013 release, reproduced at https://www.2luxury2.com/?p=45214 and https://www.supercars.net/blog/?p=370141); 963 x 0.98632 = 950 hp

weightCandidates.source: 1,255 kg dry (supercars.net, rossoautomobili.com); not seen on a Ferrari page
1,410 kg, Motor Sport, Andrew Frankel: 'a proper, comparable with fluids kerb weight' https://www.motorsportmagazine.com/archive/article/july-2014/62/laferrari
1,430 kg, MOTOR (Australia) spec panel, Georg Kacher https://whichcar.com.au/reviews/ferrari-laferrari-review

cars.notes: 499 built; calendar years 2013-2016 from one unsigned source. US model years not sourced. 3 October 2026 provisional pass: KBB 2,976 lb vs magazines 1,410-1,430 kg (3,109-3,153 lb); stays held. US model years: EPA via MPG Buddy rates 2014 only; KBB also lists 2015. 5 October 2026: ultimatespecs and dimensions.com (owner) give 1,585 kg, but ultimatespecs prints the same for the Aperta, so it looks copied; 11-12% above the magazines. Would resolve: a Ferrari document with a kerb weight, or an Evo / Autocar / Car and Driver spec panel labelled kerb or curb.

cars.missing: Any Tesla horsepower rating and curb weight; Tesla did not publish hp for these years.
cars.notes: 3 October 2026 provisional pass: horsepower sources disagree widely (450-487 hp) and 2021 weights disagree (Cars.com 4,250 vs KBB 4,065 lb); stays held. 2018 weight 4,072 lb (Cars.com and KBB) agrees. 5 October 2026: the owner's 510 hp is for the new (2024 on, 'Highland') Performance, now a separate provisional record (tesla-model-3-performance-highland). This 2018-2023 car still has no Tesla hp rating.

cars.missing: Rivian horsepower and any qualifying curb weight.
cars.notes: MotorWeek: 835 hp total. 3 October 2026 provisional pass: weights disagree by 2.9% (7,148 vs 6,949 lb); 835 hp everywhere but no Rivian page. A future record should cover only the Gen 1 Quad (2022-2024). 5 October 2026: 7,148 lb (AutoPadre, owner) is Edmunds' scale weight from its 2021 test ('The R1T weighed in at 7,148 pounds'), applied by AutoPadre to every trim; 6,949 lb (dimensions.com) is unsourced. Would resolve: Rivian's own curb weight for the 2022-2024 R1T Quad-Motor, or a magazine spec panel giving curb (not tested) weight.

cars.missing: A decision and a weight. The SS was a package on the Z28 (Edmunds: 'The SS version of the Z28 makes 320 horsepower'); only Supercars.net gives SS figures (320 bhp, 3,360 lb, unsourced). For the Z28 instead, weights disagree by more than 2% (KBB 3,306, Cars.com 3,446, Encycarpedia 3,428 lb).
cars.notes: Z28 power: 305 hp (KBB, Cars.com). 5 October 2026: the Z28 (1998-2002) is now its own provisional record. SS weights still disagree (Edmunds 3,442, The Auto Channel 3,439, encyCARpedia 3,472, Supercars.net 3,360 lb) and the 2001 rating is 320 or 325 hp depending on the source. Would resolve: a GM/Chevrolet or SLP 1998-2002 Camaro SS spec sheet or brochure, or a magazine spec panel, with the SS curb weight and the 2001 rating.
